title: Add mixed-workload scheduler dashboards (queueing metrics + tail breakdown panels)
author: Felix Schneider
body:
Title: Add mixed-workload scheduler dashboards (queueing metrics + tail breakdown panels)

Context: The mixed-workload scheduler prototype introduces short/long class queues and new scheduler decision telemetry. During perf-canary and limited prod rollouts we need a consistent set of panels that (a) confirm the policy is reducing short/interactive p95/p99 latency under long-prompt contention and (b) make starvation/backlog regressions obvious early. This PR adds reusable dashboard templates to observability-pack so SRE + runtime teams can pin a standard view during canaries and ongoing monitoring.

What’s in this PR: Adds Grafana dashboard JSON templates and generated dashboards for Mixed-Workload Scheduler monitoring. The dashboard is split into three sections: (1) Queueing + fairness (queue depth, wait time, service time by class, starvation guardrails), (2) Tail breakdown (end-to-end p95/p99 broken into queue wait vs prefill vs decode where available), (3) Saturation + overload signals (GPU/utilization + batching signals + admission control/drops if enabled). Panels are parameterized by cluster, region, route, model, and scheduler flag state where labels exist.

Key panels and queries (high level): Queue depth by class (short/long): rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{class=…}; Queue wait time (p50/p95/p99) by class: rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucket (histogram); Service time split (prefill/decode) by class: rw_runtime_request_stage_seconds_bucket{stage=prefill|decode,class=…}; Starvation guardrail: long class max wait (p99) + a single-stat for long class age vs configured max_wait_s; Tail breakdown: p95 e2e latency overlaid with p95 queue wait + p95 prefill + p95 decode (where stage metrics present) to make it obvious if improvements are coming from queueing vs kernel/runtime; Overload/backpressure: admission rejects by class (if emitted) + request timeout rate; Canary comparison helper row: side-by-side panels with scheduler_flag=on vs off for the same route/model (requires label present from canary job / environment variable injection).

Notes on metric naming: This PR assumes the runtime PRs land the following names/labels (or equivalent via relabeling): rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth gauge with class label; rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds histogram with class label; rw_runtime_scheduler_dequeue_total counter with class label; rw_runtime_request_stage_seconds histogram with stage + class labels; rw_runtime_scheduler_starvation_events_total counter with class label. If any of these names shift before runtime-1.19, we should either update the templates here or add a short-term relabel mapping in the ingest pipeline.

Files changed (summary): dashboards/mixed-workload-scheduler/dashboard.libsonnet (new): main dashboard template; dashboards/mixed-workload-scheduler/panels/*.libsonnet (new): shared panels (queue depth, wait hist, tail breakdown, saturation row, canary compare row); dashboards/generated/mixed-workload-scheduler.json (new): rendered dashboard artifact for import; dashboards/README.md (updated): how to render + import generated dashboards; tooling/render_dashboards.sh (updated): include new dashboard in render list.

How to test: 1) Run ./tooling/render_dashboards.sh and confirm no diff after render; 2) Import dashboards/generated/mixed-workload-scheduler.json into a test Grafana workspace; 3) Point variables (cluster/route/model) at a perf-canary environment with the scheduler instrumentation enabled; 4) Validate panels populate and histograms render with expected percentiles.

Screenshots/preview: Not attached (internal Grafana links in comments below), but the generated JSON is included for a stable importable artifact.

Review conversation (highlights): Aisha Bello (SRE): Requested an explicit starvation row with a paging-friendly signal and a panel that makes backlog growth obvious under burst. Update: added “Long queue age (p99) vs max_wait_s” + “Queue depth derivative” row, and a note on suggested alert thresholds in panel descriptions. Allison Grant: Asked to avoid hardcoding metric names in panel titles and to keep label filters consistent with standards (cluster, env, region, route, model). Update: standardized variables and moved metric names to panel query descriptions instead of titles. Omar El-Sayed: Pointed out that stage histograms may not exist in all environments initially; requested graceful degradation. Update: tail breakdown panels now show e2e latency alone if stage series are absent (using Grafana “null as zero” disabled and “hide series when no data” where supported). Chloe Martin: Requested alignment with Console foldering/naming conventions. Update: dashboard title and tags now match “Runtime / Scheduling / Mixed Workload”. Sean Gallagher: Requested a canary-specific row to quickly compare baseline vs flag-on during rollout windows. Update: added “Canary compare” row (requires scheduler_flag label injected by canary job).

CI: grafana-json-lint (pass); dashboards-render (pass); unit (pass); one initial failure on dashboards-render due to missing include in render script (fixed in 5a2c7d2).

Release/rollout: No product release notes. This is a template-only change; safe to land ahead of runtime-1.19. SRE can pin this dashboard during ENG-4829 canary and use it as the default view for mixed-workload investigations.

Related: Linear ENG-4828 (dashboard panels), ENG-4824 (scheduler metrics); Runtime PRs that add/confirm metrics: redwood/pr_8444 (scheduler instrumentation) and follow-ups for starvation guardrails.

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main.
